title: Mila and Pip's Pie Chart Goal
markdown:
Mila the inventor sighed. Beside her, Pip the fox thumped his tail. The school’s Bright Ideas Fair was coming, and they needed two hundred dollars for art supplies. Their lemonade stand had earned fifty. The goal felt tall.

They found Dr Rowan in her garden. Mila showed the tracker. “We’ve only raised fifty out of two hundred.”

Rowan smiled, still kneeling among the beans. “Think of two hundred as a whole pizza. Fifty dollars is one slice, if the pizza had four equal slices. That’s one-quarter. If we imagine a hundred slices, your fifty is twenty-five of them. We call that twenty-five percent. It means out of a hundred.” A bee moved from flower to flower. “Each flower is a little part of the meadow, the way your fifty is a part of the two hundred.”

Mila’s eyes lit. “So fifty out of two hundred is twenty-five percent. A good chunk of the pie. Pip — we can make posters. Show people how much of the pie we’ve got, and how much is left.”

The next day their lemonade stand wore colour. One poster showed a pie with a quarter gone: We’ve eaten 25% of our goal. Help us finish the pie. Another was a thermometer: We need $200. Currently $50 (25%). Let’s reach 50% ($100) today.

People stopped. They could see the missing slice, and the missing slice was easier to help than a mountain of two hundred. A ten-dollar donation made the pie grow: sixty out of two hundred — thirty percent. Another twenty dollars brought them to eighty — forty percent, not a guess, a slice they could colour in. The charts made the climb visible. Coins, notes, a neighbour’s extra jar. By the end of the day the thermometer had reached the top. Two hundred dollars. A whole pie.

Back in the garden they showed Rowan the full chart. Pip barked, happy enough to forget dignity.

“You used percentages to show progress,” Rowan said. “Parts of a whole — a pizza, a fundraiser, how much of the day is left for adventures.”

Mila was already sketching a new tracker, slices marked in tens. Pip nudged her hand.

“I wonder,” he said, “what else we could cut into a hundred pieces and still call a whole.”

The bee had moved on. The posters dried in the sun, their last slice finally filled in, and Mila, with her inventor’s heart, left a blank page for whatever they measured next.
characters: Mila (a careful inventor), Pip (a fox), Rowan (a scientist)
author: StoryGen Community
